name: Dot-pattern livery
description: White fuselage with the gray 'vueling' wordmark behind the forward door; a halftone of dark-gray dots, growing larger toward the tail, covers the fin and wraps the aft fuselage behind the wing, with one yellow dot high on the fin; bright yellow engines with 'vueling.com'; yellow sharklets; dark gray tail cone.

The wordmark with '.com' along the yellow cowling.

notes: The halftone (dots growing from small at the front of each field to large at the back) can't be drawn as flat areas: it's given as two average tones; a renderer could draw dots instead. Recent (2024–26) Commons photos weren't found for this pass, so the 2018–2022 photos stand in. The belly under the aft field isn't seen. Re-checked 2026-11-15: the title measured on EC-NAJ (A320neo, side-on, 2022; it wears a 'We love places' decal special, the title as on the standard) and sized against EC-MYB (2018): it runs x 0.153-0.235, its baseline just above the window tops and its ascenders about 0.5 m tall, smaller and higher than drawn; lowercase 0.65 of the l. The halftone fields' forward edges reduced to their ends (straight from the side). Still no 2024-26 standard photo on Commons.
history: Replaces Skyarium v1's approximation. The dot-pattern scheme replaced Vueling's earlier white-and-yellow scheme with the large gray-and-yellow tail lettering; the year it was introduced isn't confirmed here.
